$comment: Tables referenced by server SQL that NOTHING in the repo creates — no migration, no drizzle pgTable, no runtime DDL. Pinned to the exact referencing file set, so an entry cannot silently acquire new call sites. Every entry is a feature that either returns 500 (unguarded query) or silently no-ops (query inside try/catch). Each is a defect awaiting a code-derived migration or a retirement, NOT an approved pattern. Shrink this file; never grow it. See ledger C-11/C-14 for the remediation pattern: derive the shape from the queries, add one canonical migration, prove it with a golden journey.
$note_on_the_2026_09_10_entries: The reg_* entries (reg_submissions, reg_changes, reg_ectd_packages) are NOT newly broken. They were added on 2026-09-10 (WO-1) when server/schema/regulatory.sql was archived to sql/_legacy/ — a hand-written dump that NO applier runs and that nothing in the repo references. This guard counted that file as a creator, so the six server files querying those tables looked backed. They were not: none of reg_programs / reg_submissions / reg_requirements / reg_tasks / reg_changes / reg_ectd_packages / reg_policies / reg_policy_violations / reg_ai_recommendations / reg_workflow_instances / reg_checklists exists on a database built from empty by scripts/db/provision-test-db.sh. So server/api/cmc/portfolio.ts, server/routes/cmc-module3-board.routes.ts, server/services/documentExportService.ts, server/src/services/integrations/gmail.ts and server/src/services/reg/rpi.ts query relations that have never existed on any provisioned database. Archiving the file did not break them; it stopped the guard from hiding them. Fixing them is product work — a code-derived migration, or retiring the queries — and belongs in its own work order, not in a schema-deduplication change.
